  "content": "# Fable 5.1 narrow preexecution addendum (plan: write to deliverables/bounded-k-2026-09-09/fable-k-preexecution-addendum.md)

## Context
Prior full review approved the bounded K candidate with finding 1 (`klabel` alone probably fails closed on label mangling). The author replaced all 10 `[klabel(name)]` with `[symbol(name)]` in `moriarty.k` only, ran `kompile -O0 --help` at the pinned version (exit 0), and captured a cgroup preflight receipt. This addendum states whether approval and the resource vote extend.

## Verdict
- Approval and resource vote **extend** to `moriarty.k` at SHA `c4eedd0e…1070a`, subject to one blocker below. Reading review only; no hashes computed, nothing executed.

## Blocker (must clear before dispatch)
- The supplied `candidate.json` still lists `moriarty.k` at the old SHA `0e695ac5…14cd`. The preflight condition "verify manifest hashes against the worktree" fails closed against the new file. Regenerate `candidate.json` with the new digest (no other entry changes) before preflight. This is a manifest bookkeeping fix, not a candidate change.

## Confirmed by reading
- Exactly 10 productions changed, all to `symbol(name)`: balance, allowance, obligation, work, transfer, repay, packet, pending, rejected, prepared. No rule, sort, arity, or guard text differs from the reviewed candidate.
- No `klabel(_)` remains, so the manual's co-occurrence prohibition is not triggered.
- Manual excerpt: `symbol(_)` sets the exact identifier; frontend and KAST label become the literal name. `codec.py` requires literal `rejected` / `prepared`, so prior finding 1 is resolved as designed.
- The 10 names do not collide with any symbol in INT, BOOL, STRING, or the K prelude; uniqueness enforcement should not fire.
- `inspect`, `finish`, `ensure` keep generated labels; the codec never inspects them because `<k>` is emptied on both paths.
- Cgroup receipt shows `memory.max` 4294967296 and `memory.swap.max` 0 on a user-slice service unit, satisfying the enforcement preflight. Same properties apply to the dispatch unit.

## Residual notes (not blockers)
- `kompile -O0 --help` exiting 0 is weak evidence that `-O0` is accepted; picocli may print help before rejecting unmatched options. If the captured help text lists `-O0`, treat it as confirmed; otherwise the first compile still carries a small flag-rejection risk that fails closed.
- The manual excerpt is current, not version-pinned. `symbol(_)` predates 7.1.337, so risk is low.
- Prior findings 2 through 6 stand unchanged, including the parser-cache `COMPILED_STALE` fail-closed signature.

## Verification
- After regenerating `candidate.json`, rerun the read-only manifest hash check; expect a match for `moriarty.k` at `c4eedd0e…1070a` and all other entries unchanged.
